S2_thermal_testing.rule_summary: Each battery model must undergo independent 55 °C sustained-heat testing under a regulator-approved protocol before sale and after a material design change. A failure rate above 5% requires prompt regulator notification and a regulator-approved corrective-action plan, with follow-up testing on a defined timetable; it does not by itself require an automatic sales ban.
S2_thermal_testing.final_rule_text: Each battery model must undergo independent 55 °C sustained-heat testing under a regulator-approved protocol before sale and after a material design change. A failure rate above 5% requires prompt regulator notification and a regulator-approved corrective-action plan, with follow-up testing on a defined timetable; it does not by itself require an automatic sales ban. Manufacturers must submit per-model results, protocol, sample size, and corrective actions to the regulator. Before purchase, customers must receive the tested model’s failure rate and clear safety instructions, material risks, and relevant corrective actions. Regulators must protect identifiable per-model test results from public release, while being able to publish aggregated results. This does not limit disclosure of identifiable per-model results to customers considering purchase of that model.

parameters.quote: New units must include a remote emergency shut-off capability that can be activated by the owner and, when necessary to address an imminent safety hazard, by the manufacturer or emergency responders under a documented procedure. Manufacturers must provide a secure software or hardware retrofit for installed units lacking this capability, completing the retrofit within 6 years of this standard taking effect.

S3_remote_shutoff.rule_summary: New units must include a remote emergency shut-off capability that can be activated by the owner and, when necessary to address an imminent safety hazard, by the manufacturer or emergency responders under a documented procedure. Manufacturers must provide a secure software or hardware retrofit for installed units lacking this capability, completing the retrofit within 6 years of this standard taking effect.
S3_remote_shutoff.final_rule_text: New units must include a remote emergency shut-off capability that can be activated by the owner and, when necessary to address an imminent safety hazard, by the manufacturer or emergency responders under a documented procedure. Manufacturers must provide a secure software or hardware retrofit for installed units lacking this capability, completing the retrofit within 6 years of this standard taking effect. The shut-off must not prevent safe local operation or emergency isolation.

parameters.quote: New units must include built-in fire suppression for units manufactured 36 months after this standard is adopted.

S4_fire_suppression.rule_summary: New units must include built-in fire suppression for units manufactured 36 months after this standard is adopted.
S4_fire_suppression.final_rule_text: New units must include built-in fire suppression for units manufactured 36 months after this standard is adopted. The system must be independently tested for effectiveness and must not create an additional material safety hazard. Manufacturers must provide installation and maintenance instructions and disclose any limitations to customers.

parameters.quote: Manufacturers must notify affected customers promptly of newly identified hazards and provide clear instructions for safe use, repair, or shutdown. A model must be recalled when its thermal incident rate exceeds 8 incidents per 100,000 installed units in any year; the manufacturer must promptly notify regulators and affected customers, stop new sales, and provide a timely repair, replacement, or refund plan.

S5_customer_disclosure.rule_summary: Manufacturers must notify affected customers promptly of newly identified hazards and provide clear instructions for safe use, repair, or shutdown. A model must be recalled when its thermal incident rate exceeds 8 incidents per 100,000 installed units in any year; the manufacturer must promptly notify regulators and affected customers, stop new sales, and provide a timely repair, replacement, or refund plan.
S5_customer_disclosure.final_rule_text: Before purchase, customers must receive the model’s per-model thermal test results, safety instructions, known material risks, and any relevant incident or corrective-action notices. Manufacturers must notify affected customers promptly of newly identified hazards and provide clear instructions for safe use, repair, or shutdown. A model must be recalled when its thermal incident rate exceeds 8 incidents per 100,000 installed units in any year; the manufacturer must promptly notify regulators and affected customers, stop new sales, and provide a timely repair, replacement, or refund plan.

judge_section_notes: The final rules are strict on reporting (S1) and recall (S5), with mandatory recall at 8/100k and prompt customer notices. S2 requires 55 °C testing and a 5% threshold but only corrective action, not a sales ban, and gives numeric results to customers while shielding them from public release. S3 requires new-unit shut-off and a 6-year retrofit; S4 requires built-in suppression at 36 months.
